--- title: "Multiple Regression and Interaction" subtitle: "Introduction to Global Health Data Science" date: "2026-10-26" format: revealjs: output-file: w09-01-multreg-interact-slides.html footer: "[🔗 sta198-fa26-2.github.io](https://sta198-fa26-2.github.io/)" theme: slides.scss transition: fade slide-number: true pdf-separate-fragments: true toc: false html: code-link: true filters: - ../remove-fmt-skip.lua editor_options: chunk_output_type: console --- ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(tidymodels) library(ggtext) library(knitr) library(kableExtra) options(dplyr.print_min = 10, dplyr.print_max = 6) mercury <- readr::read_csv("../data/mercury_reg.csv") mercury <- mercury %>% # scale() subtracts the mean and divides by the SD to make the units "standard deviations" like a z-score mutate(assets_sc=scale(SESassets)) %>% #another variable we may use later mutate(form_min_sc=scale(FM_buffer)) %>% #so I don't have to remember coding mutate(sex,sex_cat=ifelse(sex==1,"Male","Female")) %>% mutate(native,native_cat=ifelse(native==1,"Native","Non-native")) # limit to one observation per household (household ID=1) mercury1 <- mercury %>% filter(withinid==1) ``` ::: # The linear model with multiple predictors ## Multiple explanatory variables
We previously explored how the relationship between assets and mercury in hair depended on whether a person lives in a native community.
::: {.panel-tabset} ## Plot :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="20%"}
::: {.question} How, if at all, does the relationship between hair mercury and household assets of individuals vary by whether or not they live in a town classified as native? :::
::: ::: {.column width="80%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w09-01-multreg-interact_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){fig-align='center' width=70%} ::: ::: ::: {.fragment}
This is an example of an interaction effect -- the relationship between assets and mercury depends on the value of a third variable, community type.
::: ::: :::: ## Code ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data = mercury, aes(x = assets_sc, y = lhairHg, color = native_cat)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.1) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) + labs( title = "Hair mercury as a function of assets, by village type", subtitle = "Peruvian Amazon", x = "Household assets (standardized)", y = "Hair mercury (log ppm)", color = NULL ) + scale_color_manual(values = c("#E48957", "#071381")) ``` ::: ::: ## Multiple explanatory variables Code to fit this model is given below. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} linear_reg() %>% set_engine("lm") %>% fit(lhairHg ~ assets_sc + native_cat + assets_sc*native_cat, data = mercury) %>% tidy() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 × 5 term estimate std.error statistic p.value 1 (Intercept) 0.845 0.0575 14.7 9.93e-47 2 assets_sc -0.295 0.0430 -6.85 9.33e-12 3 native_catNon-native -0.807 0.0626 -12.9 9.10e-37 4 assets_sc:native_catNon-… 0.217 0.0519 4.18 2.99e- 5 ``` ::: ::: ## todo Amy this is from the multiple regression part of the first diagnostics lecture in 2022 I fixed up the simple regression notes with more details, so now I can build from here. You need the interaction. we can evaluate that, and interpret the different lines. Then add a predictor for which we don't need an interaction -- in an old set of notes at the end I think w08-02 or w08-01 or w08-03 i have a good fitting big model - see next slides ## {background-color="white"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} fit <- linear_reg() %>% set_engine("lm") %>% fit(lhairHg ~ native_cat+age+assets_sc+sex_cat+native_cat*assets_sc, data = mercury) fit %>% tidy(exponentiate=TRUE,conf.int=TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 7 term estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low conf.high 1 (Inte… 1.84 0.0673 9.08 2.25e-19 1.61 2.10 2 nativ… 0.450 0.0619 -12.9 8.48e-37 0.399 0.508 3 age 1.01 0.00123 7.50 9.10e-14 1.01 1.01 4 asset… 0.747 0.0426 -6.86 9.14e-12 0.687 0.812 5 sex_c… 1.00 0.0415 0.0563 9.55e- 1 0.924 1.09 6 nativ… 1.22 0.0513 3.91 9.42e- 5 1.11 1.35 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} fit %>% glance() %>% print(width = Inf) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 12 r.squared adj.r.squared sigma statistic p.value df logLik 1 0.227 0.225 0.952 135. 2.54e-125 5 -3144.     function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
